title: Comparison between Early Clinical Results of Dual-Linear and Conventional Foot-Pedal Control in Phacoemulsification

indication: Bilateral cataract, LOCS III nuclear opalescence NO2-NO6, patients older than 45 years; prior ocular surgery or trauma, corneal disorders, uncontrolled glaucoma, zonular weakness and ECC < 1500 cells/mm2 excluded

groups.description: Study group: phacoemulsification (Stellaris Elite, 2.0 mm clear corneal incision, pre-chop, multiple burst mode) with dual-linear foot-pedal control (pitch for phaco power, yaw for vacuum) and adaptive fluidics (bottle 65 cm); one eye of each patient, first operated eye randomly assigned
Control group: the same surgeon and technique with conventional pitch-only foot-pedal control and gravity infusion (bottle 70-80 cm); the operated contralateral eye of the same patients

notes: Retrospective paired-eye contralateral study (94 patients, 188 eyes); both eyes were operated, so the contralateral conventional eye is an operated arm, not an unoperated fellow eye; the two arms are not independent samples.

Role: the authors' 'study group' (dual-linear foot-pedal control with adaptive fluidics) is the investigational technique variant (treated); conventional foot-pedal control is the standard arm (control). Fluidics also differed between arms (adaptive vs gravity infusion).
Patients who missed routine postoperative visits were excluded (Methods); Table 5 does not state per-visit n.
One surgeon; the dual-linear cases were the surgeon's first experience with that pedal control (Discussion).
